title: Maintain turf cricket pitches and outfields

lessons.title: The pitch and the outfield
lessons.html:
What a groundsman looks after

A cricket field has two very different areas. The square in the middle holds the pitches. The outfield is the large grassed area around it. In South Africa most fields use warm-season grasses such as kikuyu or couch (Cynodon) on the outfield, and couch on the square.

The pitch

  • A pitch is 22 yards (about 20.12 m) between the stumps.
  • It is made of clay loam that is rolled very hard so the ball bounces evenly.
  • Grass on the pitch is cut very short for matches.
  • The ends where bowlers land and batters stand get the most wear.

The outfield

  • Should be level, firm and smooth, with even grass, so the ball runs true.
  • Must drain well so play can start soon after rain.
  • No holes, stones, sprinkler heads sticking up or dangerous objects.

Daily and weekly tasks

TaskPitchOutfield
MowingCylinder mower, very low, oftenCylinder or rotary mower, higher cut
RollingHeavy roller to prepare and hardenLight rolling only when needed
WateringControlled; soak then dry out before a matchRegular, to keep grass green
MarkingCreases painted before each matchBoundary rope or line

The head groundsman decides what is done. You follow the work plan and tell him or her about any problem you see, such as dry patches, pests or damage.

lessons.title: Preparing a pitch and renovating after the season
lessons.html:
Match pitch preparation

Pitch preparation usually starts about 10 to 14 days before a match. The head groundsman sets the plan. A typical pattern is:

  1. Brush and cut the grass, reducing the height of cut step by step.
  2. Water deeply so the clay is moist all the way down.
  3. Roll when the surface is firm enough not to stick to the roller. Start with a light roller and move to the heavy roller. Roll in straight lines, end to end.
  4. Dry out slowly. Cover with pitch covers if rain is coming.
  5. Final cut and roll the day before and the morning of the match.
  6. Mark the creases with a string line, frame and white line paint, to the exact measurements given.

During a match

  • Bring on covers quickly when it rains. Work as a team.
  • Sweep and roll between innings only as the rules and the umpires allow.
  • Repair bowlers' footholes after play with the right clay, packed in firmly.

End of season renovation

  1. Scarify (rake out dead grass and thatch) hard.
  2. Spike or core the surface to let in air and water.
  3. Top-dress with the same clay loam, worked into the holes and levelled.
  4. Fertilise and water to get grass to grow back.
  5. Repair worn outfield areas with sods or seed.

Safety

  • Only drive a roller or mower you are trained on. Keep people away from moving rollers.
  • Wear ear protection and safety boots.
  • Never work on the square while play is on.
  • Stop work when there is lightning. Open fields are dangerous in storms.

Key points

  • The square needs precise mowing, watering and rolling; the outfield needs to be level, firm and well drained.
  • Roll only when the surface does not stick to the roller.
  • Get covers on quickly when rain comes.
  • Renovate at season end: scarify, spike, top-dress, feed and water.
  • Use machines only when trained and stop work in lightning.
